answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain custody of 1,000 unique data shards as a digital vault, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits to ensure active storage capacity. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct files across the network. A verifier requests random segments at the dawn of each epoch to prevent data reuse. Acting like a sparrow foraging for hidden grains, the verifier audits data integrity, where any failure triggers a non-refundable slash to funds.
